History:
- Main complaint: Generalized body aches and significant fatigue/rundown for ~6 weeks (possibly longer).
- Onset/progression: Felt well around Christmas/New Year; symptoms began a couple of weeks after returning from a U.S. holiday (trip end Jan/early Feb). Persistent since then.
- Associated symptoms: Decreased appetite/early satiety (smaller portions, effort to finish meals) without reported weight change; occasional mild headache; no sore throat currently.
- Prior episode: Transient rash on posterior calf noted mid–late February, minimally itchy, resolved over ~2 weeks. Around that time, had a mild sore throat and possibly felt mildly feverish.
- Negatives: No persistent URI symptoms, ear pain, cough, shortness of breath, phlegm; no dysphagia, heartburn, abdominal pain; no diarrhea, vomiting, blood in stool; no urinary symptoms or hematuria; no blurred vision, tingling, or numbness.
- Musculoskeletal: Diffuse aching (shoulders, back, hips, knees); no joint swelling reported.
- Function: Attending work but with reduced energy/concentration; decreased exercise compared to baseline.
- Context/exposures: Extensive walking while on holiday, wore shorts; does not recall any bites; lives with wife.
- Mental health: Currently good; prior history of issues but stable now.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Hay fever (allergic rhinitis).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications:
  - Preventive inhaler for asthma (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Over-the-counter antihistamine (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Tobacco: Not documented.
- Alcohol: Occasional use (conflict noted: clinician initially said “No,” patient clarified “occasionally”).
- Hospitalizations/surgeries: Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals obtained.
- Skin: No current rash reported; prior transient calf rash resolved.
- Joints: No swelling reported.
- General: Able to converse; no acute respiratory symptoms reported.

Impression:
- Subacute fatigue with generalized myalgias/arthralgias; possible Lyme disease given transient calf rash after outdoor exposure, with workup planned; other common causes of fatigue to be evaluated with baseline labs.

Management Plan:
- Laboratory tests: Order blood tests including complete blood count, renal and liver function tests, and Lyme disease serology.
- If Lyme serology positive: Start appropriate antibiotic therapy (to be determined based on result).
- Logistics: Patient to book blood draw via support line; arrange follow-up about one week after labs are completed (telephone follow-up acceptable).
- No immediate medication changes documented.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with ~6 weeks of fatigue and diffuse body aches beginning after a U.S. trip, with a resolved transient calf rash noted mid–late February. Lyme disease is being considered alongside other routine causes of fatigue; labs (CBC, renal/liver, Lyme serology) have been arranged. Follow-up planned after results to determine treatment.

Key Takeaways:
- Get the ordered blood tests (CBC, kidney/liver panel, Lyme serology).
- Lyme disease is a consideration due to the prior rash and outdoor exposure; antibiotics may be required if tests are positive.
- Schedule and attend a phone follow-up about one week after completing the tests.

Next Steps:
- Book and complete blood tests via the support line.
- Monitor symptoms; seek earlier care if worsening significantly (not specifically discussed in consult).
- Telephone follow-up in ~1 week after labs to review results and plan treatment if indicated.

- Internal conflicts: Alcohol use—clinician said “No,” patient clarified “occasionally” (conflict noted; patient’s statement used).
